## PCI PM callback call chains

The PCI driver’s PM callbacks are registered through the driver’s `dev_pm_ops` in **`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`**. The suspend-side callbacks resolve as follows:

```text
PCI PM suspend
  └─ i915_pm_suspend(dev)
       └─ i915_drm_suspend(dev)
            ├─ pdev = to_pci_dev(dev)
            ├─ dev_priv = pdev_to_i915(pdev)
            ├─ intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)
            ├─ i915_gem_suspend(dev_priv)
            ├─ intel_gt_suspend(dev_priv)
            ├─ intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)
            └─ intel_uncore_suspend(dev_priv)
```

```text
PCI PM freeze
  └─ i915_pm_freeze(dev)
       └─ i915_drm_suspend(dev)
            └─ [same suspend sequence]
```

```text
PCI PM poweroff
  └─ i915_pm_poweroff(dev)
       └─ i915_drm_suspend(dev)
            └─ [same suspend sequence]
```

The resume-side callbacks do not reach `i915_pm_suspend`:

```text
PCI PM resume
  └─ i915_pm_resume(dev)
       └─ i915_drm_resume(dev)
```

```text
PCI PM thaw
  └─ i915_pm_thaw(dev)
       └─ i915_drm_resume(dev)
```

```text
PCI PM restore
  └─ i915_pm_restore(dev)
       └─ i915_drm_resume(dev)
```

Thus, strictly speaking, only the normal suspend callback enters `i915_pm_suspend`; freeze and poweroff are sibling callbacks that enter the common lower-level function `i915_drm_suspend` directly. The complete suspend-side set is:

| PCI PM callback | Common suspend function reached |
|---|---|
| `i915_pm_suspend()` | `i915_drm_suspend()` |
| `i915_pm_freeze()` | `i915_drm_suspend()` |
| `i915_pm_poweroff()` | `i915_drm_suspend()` |

Relevant implementation areas are **`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c`**, **`i915_driver.h`**, **`gem/i915_gem_pm.c`**, **`gt/intel_gt_pm.c`**, **`intel_uncore.c`**, and **`display/intel_display_driver.c`**.

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None of the PCI system-sleep callbacks above call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`.

Runtime suspend is a separate PM path:

```text
PCI runtime PM
  └─ i915_pm_runtime_suspend(dev)
       ├─ dev_priv = pdev_to_i915(to_pci_dev(dev))
       ├─ i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
       ├─ intel_gt_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
       ├─ intel_display_power_suspend(dev_priv)
       └─ runtime power-management / uncore handling
```

It is installed independently as the `.runtime_suspend` callback in the PM operations table. There is no callback in the suspend/freeze/poweroff family that invokes it, and `i915_pm_runtime_suspend()` does not invoke `i915_pm_suspend()` either.

## `dev_priv` data flow

The pointer flow from the device-model callback to display suspend is:

```text
struct device *dev
       │
       ▼
to_pci_dev(dev)
       │
       ▼
struct pci_dev *pdev
       │
       ▼
pdev_to_i915(pdev)
       │
       ▼
struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
       │
       ▼
intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)
```

In `i915_drm_suspend()`:

1. The PM callback receives the generic `struct device *dev`.
2. `to_pci_dev(dev)` recovers the enclosing `struct pci_dev`.
3. `pdev_to_i915(pdev)` obtains the driver-private `struct drm_i915_private *`.
4. That same pointer is passed directly to `intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)`.
5. `intel_display_suspend()` uses `dev_priv` to access the display runtime state, display power domains, modeset state, and display-specific suspend hooks.

So there is no copy or intermediate allocation: `dev_priv` is derived from the PCI device and propagated unchanged into the display suspend layer.
